### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. hyperzincemia with functional zinc depletion  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.666)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:9580)

**Proposed mechanism:** PSTPIP1 (HGNC:9580) —DISRUPTS→ Regulation of T-cell activation and signaling (GO:0042110); Regulation of T-cell activation and signaling (GO:0042110) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal T-cell signaling (HP:0033131); PSTPIP1 (HGNC:9580) —DISRUPTS→ Zinc homeostasis (GO:0006470); Zinc homeostasis (GO:0006470) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperzincemia (HP:0011020). Haploinsufficiency of PSTPIP1 disrupts T-cell signaling pathways, leading to the phenotypes associated with MONDO:0011462. Concurrently, PSTPIP1 dysfunction also impacts zinc homeostasis, resulting in hyperzincemia and functional zinc depletion.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct causal genes for MONDO:0011462 and hyperzincemia with functional zinc depletion, or demonstration of divergent functional consequences of PSTPIP1 mutations in each disease. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the dual role of PSTPIP1 in immune regulation and zinc homeostasis could lead to novel therapeutic strategies for both immune-related disorders and metabolic conditions like hyperzincemia.

#### 2. hearing loss, autosomal dominant 34, with or without inflammation  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.485)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9660826, Reactome:R-HSA-844456)

**Proposed mechanism:** Gain-of-function variant in PSTPIP1 (HGNC:9000) —DISRUPTS→ PSTPIP1 (HGNC:9000); PSTPIP1 (HGNC:9000) —INCREASES→ NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032455); NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032455) —PRODUCES→ IL-1beta (UniProtKB:P01584); IL-1beta (UniProtKB:P01584) —LEADS_TO→ Inflammation (HP:0011420); Gain-of-function variant in NLRP3 (HGNC:7641) —DISRUPTS→ NLRP3 (HGNC:7641); NLRP3 (HGNC:7641) —INCREASES→ NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032455); NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032455) —LEADS_TO→ Hearing impairment (HP:0000365). Gain-of-function variants in PSTPIP1 (associated with disease A, likely autoinflammatory conditions) and NLRP3 (associated with disease B, hearing loss with inflammation) both lead to hyperactivation of the NLRP3 inflammasome. This inflammasome activation results in the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines like IL-1beta, driving systemic inflammation and potentially contributing to the observed phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of evidence for NLRP3 inflammasome activation in patients with either disease, or demonstration that PSTPIP1 variants do not affect inflammasome activity, or that NLRP3 variants do not impact hearing. _(variant: rs1261004805 (a known pathogenic GOF variant in NLRP3))_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the NLRP3 inflammasome pathway with small molecule inhibitors or anti-cytokine therapies could offer a shared therapeutic strategy for both diseases, particularly for managing the inflammatory components and potentially mitigating hearing loss.

#### 3. Muckle-Wells syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.461)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9660826, Reactome:R-HSA-844456)

**Proposed mechanism:** PSTPIP1 (HGNC:9633) —DISRUPTS→ NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670); NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670) —LEADS_TO→ Pyogenic arthritis (HP:0005805); NLRP3 (HGNC:7695) —DISRUPTS→ NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670); NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670) —DECREASES→ Pro-IL-1 beta (UniProtKB:P01584); NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670) —PRODUCES→ Interleukin-1 beta (UniProtKB:P01584); Interleukin-1 beta (UniProtKB:P01584) —LEADS_TO→ Muckle-Wells syndrome (MONDO:0008633). Gain-of-function mutations in PSTPIP1 lead to aberrant activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, causing autoinflammatory symptoms. Similarly, gain-of-function mutations in NLRP3 itself result in excessive inflammasome activation and the characteristic phenotypes of Muckle-Wells syndrome, highlighting a shared convergence on the NLRP3 inflammasome pathway.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in PSTPIP1 do not lead to increased IL-1 beta production or inflammasome activation in relevant cellular models, or that mutations in NLRP3 do not cause Muckle-Wells syndrome. _(variant: rs79606462 (a common variant in PSTPIP1 associated with inflammatory conditions))_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the NLRP3 inflammasome pathway, for example with IL-1beta inhibitors, could offer a therapeutic strategy for both pyogenic arthritis and Muckle-Wells syndrome, given their shared mechanistic basis.

**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9660826, Reactome:R-HSA-844456)
